newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell launches training programme for Ogoni youths.
newsitem.headline: Shell launches training programme for Ogoni youths.

text.p: Shell oil company's Nigerian subsidiary said on Saturday it had begun a training programme to equip 350 Ogoni youths with skills to get jobs.
But it reiterated that it was in no hurry to resume oil operations in volatile Ogoniland in southeastern Nigeria.

"The programme is an outcome of our continuing dialogue with a cross-section of Ogoni people," the general manager of Shell in eastern Nigeria, Egbert Imomoh, said in a statement reported by the state news agency.

Shell quit Ogoniland in 1993 following sabotage of its installations by militant youths. The atmosphere became further charged in November 1995 when nine Ogoni minority rights activists including author Ken Saro-Wiwa were hanged on murdcer charges.
"We have no plans to resume operations in Ogoniland," Imomoh said, adding: "Such a step would be taken only after discussion and agreement with all Ogoni communities and opinion leaders."
The Movement for the Survival of Ogoni Peoples (MOSOP) of which Saro-Wiwa was president, had campaigned for Shell to pay compensation for environmental damage to Ogoniland.
MOSOP has now gone underground in Nigeria but issues statements out of London.

Shell said its aim was to train Ogoni youths and that the six-month programme, one of nine training initiatives planned for this year, was being run by a non-governmental organisation called Community Development Partners.
"Our priority is to provide support for the Ogoni people where we can help," Imomoh said.
Shell came under pressure from environmental groups to pull out of Nigeria because of the hanging of the nine Ogoni who were found guilty by a tribunal of the murder of four Ogoni chiefs.
But the company, which produces half of Nigeria's total output of two million barrels per day, withstood the pressure.
Shell last year took over maintenance and supply of drugs to Gokana hospital, the main medical facility in Ogoniland.
